deck_title: Brewster-Malus cross-polarizer glare extinction vs naive unpolarized specular veil washout rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Sir David Brewster (Phil. Trans. 1815) & Étienne-Louis Malus (1809) cross-polarized glare extinction (at Brewster angle theta_B = arctan(n2/n1), p-polarized Fresnel reflectance R_p(theta_B) = 0 so dielectric surface glare G_s(u) = u in [0.0000, 1.0000] is 100% s-polarized; a crossed analyzer at Delta_phi = 90 deg transmits G_s(u)*cos^2(90 deg) = 0, locking subsurface radiance ratio I_CPL / I_sub = 1.0000x across all 17 glare stations with 0/17 contaminated stations) versus naive unpolarized scalar reflection (which sums I_sub + G_s(u) = 1 + u, inflating glare-veiled radiance to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x / 50% signal purity at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Stokes-Mueller polarization propagation.
